# TestScript for 32-implicit-command
# Asserts Bun-style implicit execution and help rendering.

# 1. Bare invocation runs the parent Runner, which prints help.
exec bunlike
stdout 'Usage:\n  bunlike \[<command>\]'
stdout 'run\s+Execute a file \(default\)'
stdout 'install\s+Install dependencies'

# 2. An unmatched operand enters the implicit command.
exec bunlike ./script.ts one two
stdout 'run file=script.ts dry-run=false args=\[one two\]'

# 3. Explicit naming is equivalent.
exec bunlike run ./script.ts
stdout 'run file=script.ts dry-run=false args=\[\]'

# 4. The implicit child's flag binds before the operand.
exec bunlike -n ./script.ts
stdout 'run file=script.ts dry-run=true args=\[\]'

# 5. Explicit siblings win.
exec bunlike install
stdout 'install frozen=false'

# 6. A flag belonging only to the implicit child is invalid on a sibling.
exit-status 2 bunlike -n install
stderr 'unknown flag: -n'

# 7. Help stays parent-scoped at a bare --help request.
exec bunlike --help
stdout 'Usage:\n  bunlike \[<command>\]'
stdout 'run\s+Execute a file \(default\)'

# 8. The terminator forwards dash-prefixed operands to the implicit command.
exec bunlike -- -e.ts
stdout 'run file=-e.ts dry-run=false args=\[\]'

# 9. A builtin request before the terminator keeps parent help scope.
exec bunlike --help -- ignored.ts
stdout 'Usage:\n  bunlike \[<command>\]'
